reuse.why: Every step routes through the existing applyWeekendRule/applyWeekendRuleToDay/getDateWithSkippedWeekend helpers, and the new range handler reuses recurConfigToRSchedule and the same rule rather than writing its own weekend logic.

duplication.why: Rule logic exists once, but the four-field WeekendRule object is re-mapped at four call sites and the occurrence-window sizing exists in two separate heuristics (getOccurrenceWindow and getMaxWeekendShiftDays).

placement.why: Rule changes live in shared/schedules.ts, the handler in server/schedules/app.ts and the data fields in parseRecurDate, following the tree's layering.

scope.why: Focused on the four requests; only incidental churn such as reordering an import.

maintainability.why: A single nullable rule result keeps behaviour centralised, though every caller now has to handle null and widen its occurrence window, which spreads some awareness of the daily-skip case.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gains frequency and holidays and getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains holidays; applyWeekendRule gains a frequency === 'daily' branch returning null; all callers (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange, createScheduleList) still use the helper
